title: Plan-gate message re-injects the unsatisfiable "temporary directory means OUTSIDE this repository" guidance that 5c7f319 was supposed to eliminate
description: Commit 5c7f319 reconciled ALL guidance to one message: 'a temporary directory' is honored by an in-workspace gitignored ./scratch subdir, because the file-tool jail rejects every path outside the workspace and set_scope now refuses OUTSIDE roots (set_scope.rs:124-128 redirects to './scratch-<name>'). The entry prompt (orchestrator.rs:1836-1839, 1854-1857) and the builder hint (builder.rs:802-804) were updated — but the plan-gate error message in runner.rs was missed and still instructs the opposite: set_scope to a directory OUTSIDE the repository. This gate fires on exactly the request class involved ('je souhaite créer un CRM dans un répertoire temporaire' is wish-phrased → tier-1 plan gate on the FIRST mutation), so the harness itself steers the model into the path that set_scope then refuses and resolve_path rejects — the documented contradiction-thrash/repo-littering failure mode of live finding 6a265efd. Project memory explicitly says: do NOT re-add '/tmp'/'never in the repo' guidance.
evidence: runner.rs:2362-2366 (plan-gate ToolResult error text): "ALSO declare your working scope with set_scope (the exact target directory — honor every location constraint in the request, e.g. 'a temporary directory' means OUTSIDE this repository).{design_check} THEN build." — vs set_scope.rs:124-128 which refuses exactly that: "scope root(s) {} are OUTSIDE this workspace ({}) — the file tools can ... temporary or scratch work, scope a SUBDIRECTORY inside the workspace instead (e.g. ./scratch-<name>)"
suggested_fix: Change the plan-gate text to match the reconciled message: e.g. "— honor every location constraint in the request; 'a temporary directory' means a fresh gitignored scratch SUBDIRECTORY inside the workspace (e.g. ./scratch-<name>), since outside paths are rejected".

title: User interrupt is swallowed by the stop-gates: goal judge / verify-replan / one-shot gates run on the synthesized "[interrupted by user]" turn and continue the run instead of awaiting input
description: When the interrupt token fires mid-LLM-call, the runner synthesizes an EndTurn response and immediately re-arms the token (runner.rs:1140-1151); the design comment says "let the existing no-tool-calls path await the next on_input message". But the stop-gates (ask_gate 1697, act_gate 1728, study_contract 1756, verify-replan 1787, goal gate 1815) all run BEFORE the on_input await (1861) and none checks the `interrupted` flag (consulted only at 1161 to skip the cache put). Consequences: (a) with a goal installed (TUI set_goal / /goal — GoalSlot is live), an interrupt triggers an uninterruptible judge LLM call, the judge says not-met, and the run CONTINUES with a goal-continuation turn against the re-armed token — the user must interrupt again for each of up to max_continuations turns; (b) with replan_on_verify_fail (enabled in the TUI whenever a verify command is configured, main.rs:798/856), interrupting precisely when verify is RED — the typical reason to interrupt — makes the gate inject 'Verification is RED — do NOT finish yet' and keep the run going, consuming up to 8 interrupts; (c) in STUDY mode the study_contract gate fires once and continues the run one extra turn. The tool-batch interrupt path funnels into the same gate chain on the next turn (token left cancelled → synthesized end-of-turn → same gates).
evidence: runner.rs:1140-1151: "_ = token.cancelled() => { handle.rearm(); interrupted = true; Ok(... text: \"[interrupted by user]\" ... StopReason::EndTurn ...) }" — then runner.rs:1834-1843 (no interrupted check anywhere in the gate chain): "} else if goal_continuations_used < goal.max_continuations() { goal_continuations_used += 1; ... ctx.add_user_message(goal.continuation_message(&verdict.reason)); continue; }"
suggested_fix: Carry the `interrupted` / tool_interrupted state into the no-tool-calls branch and skip the corrective gates (replan, goal judge, ask/act/study) for an interrupted turn, falling straight through to on_input().await; alternatively check `self.interrupt` token state at the top of the gate chain.

title: Response-cache hits re-accumulate the original call's token usage: inflates total_usage, cost, budget check, and per-tenant billing for tokens never consumed
description: ResponseCache::put stores the full CompletionResponse including its original `usage` (cache.rs:58-69), and get returns it verbatim (cache.rs:44-54). On a cache hit (runner.rs:1075 `Ok(cached)`), the loop unconditionally executes `total_usage += response.usage` (1320), feeds it to the per-tenant tracker adjust (1327-1338), to per-turn cost accrual (1345-1352), and to the max_total_tokens budget check (1357-1371). So every cache hit — whose entire purpose is to cost zero — is billed as a full LLM call: usage totals and estimated_cost_usd are overstated, tenant token accounting is inflated, and a run with many cache hits can falsely trip Error::BudgetExceeded. The code is cache-hit aware right next door (TTFT comment at 1071-1073: "Stays 0 for cache hits"), so this is an oversight, not a policy.
evidence: cache.rs:47-50: "let entry = entries.remove(pos); let response = entry.1.clone(); ... Some(response)" (usage preserved) — runner.rs:1075 "let llm_result = if let Some(cached) = cache_hit { ... Ok(cached) }" then runner.rs:1320 "total_usage += response.usage;" and 1357-1369 "if let Some(max) = self.max_total_tokens { let used = total_usage.total(); if used > max { ... Error::BudgetExceeded ... } }"
suggested_fix: Zero the usage on the cached response before returning it into the loop (e.g. `cached.usage = TokenUsage::default()` at the hit site, or store responses with zeroed usage in put()).

title: Permission/approval-denied tool batches bypass doom-loop detection entirely — a model hammering a denied tool spins to max_turns with no soft warning or hard stop
description: doom_tracker.record runs at runner.rs:2094, AFTER the permission/approval stage. When every call in the batch is denied — by a permission Deny rule, by the human reviewer, or automatically by a persisted AlwaysDeny rule — the loop `continue`s at 2045-2049 (rules path) or 2069-2086 (legacy batch-approval path) without ever recording the batch. A model that re-issues the identical denied call every turn (a classic stuck pattern, and exactly what AlwaysDeny produces silently) never trips the soft doom warning nor the new DOOM_HARD_STOP_MARGIN hard abort from 9ecd8d6, and burns one LLM call per turn until max_turns (TUI chat default is 200). All the other deny-style gates (escalation_block, mode_contract, plan_gate) sit after the doom record and are correctly covered; only the permission stage is not.
evidence: runner.rs:2044-2049: "// If ALL calls were denied, add results and continue\n if allowed.is_empty() && !denied.is_empty() { total_tool_calls += denied.len(); ctx.add_tool_results(denied); continue; }" — doom recording only happens later at 2094: "if let Some(threshold) = self.max_identical_tool_calls { let (exact, fuzzy) = doom_tracker.record(&tool_calls, ...)"
suggested_fix: Record the original (pre-filter) batch in doom_tracker before the permission stage, or call doom_tracker.record on the denied batch (and check the hard-stop) before the all-denied `continue`.

title: verify-replan gate is run-scoped, not request-scoped: stale VERIFY_RESULT: FAIL from an earlier chat request re-triggers it on unrelated requests, and the 8-replan budget never resets
description: The gate scans the ENTIRE conversation for the latest canonical VERIFY_RESULT (ctx.conversation_text() renders all messages of the whole chat session; parse_latest_verify in codegen/verify.rs:86-100 takes the last canonical sentinel anywhere). In TUI chat mode (replan_on_verify_fail is enabled whenever a verify command is configured, heartbit-tui/src/main.rs:798/856), two defects follow: (1) if a request ends with the latest sentinel being FAIL (user interrupted a red build, or said 'leave it'), every subsequent natural stop on LATER unrelated requests re-fires the gate and blocks completion with 'Verification is RED — do NOT finish yet' until the model happens to produce a fresh PASS; (2) `verify_replans_used` is missing from the per-request reset block at 1905-1923 (which resets all 14 other per-request gate states), so the 8-replan budget is consumed across the whole session — after one stubborn red request, the out-of-plan protection is silently dead for the rest of the session.
evidence: runner.rs:1787-1791: "if self.replan_on_verify_fail && verify_replans_used < MAX_VERIFY_REPLANS && let Some(outcome) = crate::codegen::parse_latest_verify(&ctx.conversation_text()) && !outcome.passed" — and the new-request reset block runner.rs:1905-1923 resets nudge_tool_calls/.../study_contract_nudged but never `verify_replans_used`.
suggested_fix: Add `verify_replans_used = 0;` to the on_input reset block, and scope the verify scan to messages since the current request (e.g. record the message index at each on_input and scan only the suffix).

title: Hard escalation (advisor-required block) cannot re-arm within a request: after one advisor consult, unlimited consecutive failed builds are unblocked again
description: a2ff809's hard escalation denies edit/write/patch after ESCALATION_AFTER_FAILURES (3) consecutive failed builds until the advisor is consulted; consulting advisor clears `advisor_required` and resets the streak (runner.rs:2235-2238). But the trigger is gated on `!escalation_fired`, and `escalation_fired` is only reset on a NEW user request (1920) — never by the advisor consult. So within one request, the block can fire exactly once: after the model calls advisor, it can return to thrashing through arbitrarily many consecutive failed builds (the live finding this gate was built for was 24 consecutive failures with the advisor ignored) with no further block or escalation hint. The streak counter dutifully climbs past 3 again but `advisor_required` is never set a second time.
evidence: runner.rs:2666-2672: "consecutive_build_failures += 1; if !escalation_fired && consecutive_build_failures >= ESCALATION_AFTER_FAILURES && self.tools.contains_key(\"advisor\") { escalation_fired = true; advisor_required = true;" — and the advisor reset at runner.rs:2235-2238 clears only the block and streak: "if tool_calls.iter().any(|c| c.name == \"advisor\") { advisor_required = false; consecutive_build_failures = 0; }"
suggested_fix: Reset `escalation_fired = false` in the advisor-consult branch (2235-2238) so a fresh 3-failure streak after a consult re-raises the block, or drop the `!escalation_fired` guard and key the one-shot only on the hint text.

title: ReadOnly mode deny backstop covers only 4 tool names — delegation/MCP/A2A calls execute with side effects in STUDY/ANSWER mode
description: The mode contract has two layers: a whitelist MASK (tool_filter.rs READ_ONLY_TOOLS, lines 45-68) that filters the definitions sent to the LLM, and a deny BACKSTOP whose own comment (runner.rs:2267-2269) says it exists because 'a mutating call that slips past the masking (hallucinated name, repaired name) is refused before side effects'. But the backstop blacklist is only `["edit", "write", "patch", "bash"]`, while dispatch (runner.rs:3356 `let tool = self.tools.get(&call.name).cloned();`) executes ANY tool in the runner's full map regardless of what was masked. Tools that are masked but NOT denied: `delegate_task`, `form_squad` (entry agent, orchestrator.rs:1972/1997), `skill`, `image_generate`, `tts`, `twitter_post`, `verify`, and every MCP/A2A tool (CLI chat loads them into the same runner, heartbit-cli/src/main.rs:2507-2512). A delegated sub-agent runs with NO router (runner.rs:915 `None => super::router::RequestMode::Execute`) and full write/bash — so one exact-name `delegate_task` call in STUDY mode performs arbitrary mutations. This is made actively likely by the mode-blind DelegationNudge (orchestrator.rs:2936-2946, runner.rs:2787-2794): after 8 read-only calls in a STUDY investigation the harness injects '[delegation check] … delegate it now (delegate_task / form_squad)' — instructing the model to call a tool the mask just hid; OpenAI-compatible providers (Qwen/OpenRouter, the project's mid-tier targets) happily emit tool names from conversation history or prompt text. In `heartbit chat` (router ON by default, main.rs:2528) there is no approval callback without `--approve` (main.rs:2519-2523), so nothing else gates the call.
suggested_fix: Invert the backstop to mirror the mask: in STUDY/ANSWER, deny any call whose name is NOT in tool_filter::READ_ONLY_TOOLS (whitelist deny), instead of blacklisting 4 names. Also suppress the DelegationNudge when request_mode is Study/Answer (and arguably Clarify pre-question).

title: CLARIFY ask-first/plan-gate flags are set from the same batch's CALLS, not results — batching `question` with mutations executes writes before the user answers (and even denied batches arm the flags)
description: `question_called`, `scope_declared`, and `plan_artifact_seen` are set by scanning the CURRENT tool batch (runner.rs:2223-2234) BEFORE the mode-contract deny (2270) and plan gate (2321) evaluate them. Consequences: (1) In CLARIFY mode, a single batch `[question, set_scope, write]` (or `[question, write]` where set_scope isn't registered, e.g. CLI chat) clears `needs_ask`/`needs_scope`/`plan_artifact_seen` in the same iteration — the writes execute in the parallel JoinSet (execute_tools_parallel, line 3336) concurrently with the still-unanswered question, defeating the entire ask-first contract shipped in 322060c. This batching pattern is documented as real: the barrier-hoist comment (runner.rs:2378-2384) cites live session 6a251f55 emitting set_scope + a write in ONE batch, but only set_scope/set_goal were made barriers — `question` was not. (2) In STUDY mode, a batch `[question, write]` is wholly denied by MODE_READONLY_DENY (every call gets an error result, question never reaches the user) yet `question_called` stays true, permanently satisfying the STUDY go/no-go contract check (line 1758 `!question_called`) without any question having been asked.
suggested_fix: Evaluate needs_ask/needs_scope/plan_artifact_seen against the PRE-batch flag state (snapshot before updating), or treat `question` as a barrier tool that must complete (user answered) before sibling mutations run; only set question_called when the question tool actually executed successfully.

title: bash is not counted as a mutation by the plan gate — the CLARIFY ask-first and scope contracts never engage for bash-driven builds
description: PLAN_GATE_MUTATING is `["edit", "write", "patch"]` and the CLARIFY contracts (needs_scope from b66c39d, needs_ask from 322060c) are only consulted when `batch_mutations > 0` (runner.rs:2321). So in CLARIFY mode the model can `cargo new`, `mkdir`, and write whole files via bash heredocs (`cat > src/main.rs <<EOF`) without ever asking a question, declaring scope, or producing any plan artifact — the exact unilateral-build failure mode these gates were shipped to stop (live findings 6a258ab2/6a25947c both involved bash builds). The exclusion is deliberate per the comment, but the rationale ('a mkdir writes no content') predates and contradicts the CLARIFY ask-first contract: bash routinely writes content. Note this is DISTINCT from the accepted bash-bypasses-the-path-jail risk (option C): that acceptance covers the file-path jail, not the new mode/plan gates. MODE_READONLY_DENY does include bash for STUDY/ANSWER, so only CLARIFY is exposed. In the TUI the approval modal still asks for bash; in `heartbit chat` without --approve nothing gates it.
suggested_fix: In CLARIFY mode (at minimum), count bash calls as mutations for the needs_ask/needs_scope check — or classify bash commands (heredoc/redirect/mkdir/cargo new vs read-only) before exempting them.

title: A user-pinned STUDY/CLARIFY mode is silently overridden to EXECUTE by a bare affirmation — promotion path never consults the pin
description: The /mode pin contract is documented as absolute: the TUI notice says 'request mode PINNED to {mode} — /mode auto to release' and app.rs:1453-1455 says it 'forces the response mode for every following request', while router.rs route() short-circuits on the pin before all layers. But the bare-affirmation promotion in the runner fires on `request_mode` alone (Study|Clarify) without checking whether that mode came from a PIN: with `/mode study` pinned, the user typing 'ok' / 'oui' / 'd'accord' (e.g. acknowledging a finding mid-study) promotes that request to EXECUTE with `plan_artifact_seen`/`scope_declared` force-set true (runner.rs:1913-1914) — full mutating tool definitions restored and the plan/scope/ask gates disarmed, for a user who explicitly locked the session read-only. The pin is only re-honored on the NEXT request. is_bare_affirmation also accepts single words like 'lance', 'continue', 'sure', and strips punctuation so 'ok?' qualifies (router.rs:274-313).
suggested_fix: Before promoting, check the pin cell (expose it through RequestRouter, e.g. `router.pinned_mode()`); if a pin is active, keep the pinned mode and notify instead of promoting. Promotion should apply only to ROUTED Study/Clarify modes.

title: GO_TOKENS use whole-text substring matching — negated/embedded phrases ('don't do it yet', 'before you go ahead…') force EXECUTE at L0 confidence 1.0
description: classify_l0 checks go-tokens first via `contains_any` (plain substring over the whole lowercased message) and immediately returns Execute. Negations and incidental embeddings therefore force EXECUTE — the mode whose only contract is 'no safety nets': 'don't do it yet, first show me the plan' contains 'do it'; 'before you go ahead, explain the tradeoffs' contains 'go ahead'; FR 'tu vas y arriver' contains 'vas y'. These are realistic mid-session follow-ups to a STUDY/CLARIFY proposal, i.e. exactly when the user is saying NO — and the L0 hit (confidence 1.0) skips the L1 classifier that would read the negation. The result is the inverse of the router's design intent ('the user's keypress always wins'): the user's explicit don't-go is read as go, mutating tools stay unmasked, and only the (wish-gated) plan gate remains.
suggested_fix: Guard go-tokens against preceding negators (don't/do not/ne…pas/jamais/avant de/before you) within the same clause, or only honor go-tokens on short messages (reuse the is_bare_affirmation length/word discipline) and let longer texts fall through to the marker/classifier layers.

title: L0 read-only misroutes on common direct requests: STUDY markers match inside larger words ('analyseur', 'explorer') and any trailing '?' flips an anchored directive to ANSWER — both at confidence 1.0, skipping L1
description: Two substring/suffix heuristics misroute frequent direct requests into read-only modes where the requested mutation is then masked and denied ('[mode contract] … do not modify anything'): (1) STUDY_MARKERS are matched by substring anywhere in the text, and short stems like 'analyse', 'explore', 'évalue' match inside identifiers and ordinary words — 'corrige l'analyseur dans src/parse.rs' (contains 'analyse') and 'add tests for the explorer view in src/ui.rs' (contains 'explore') both return Study at line 234-236 despite being anchored fix/add directives; the study branch runs before every other check. (2) `interrogative` is true for ANY message ending in '?' (line 228-229, when not wish/design), so polite-imperative phrasings — 'Peux-tu corriger la typo dans src/main.rs ?', 'Can you fix the import in lib.rs?', or 'Why does the test fail? Please fix it.' — return Answer at line 238-239, read-only-masking the very edit that was requested. Both paths return with confidence 1.0, so the L1 classifier that could read the actual intent never runs. The fixture set (lines 485-546) contains no anchored-directive-with-'?' and no marker-inside-identifier case, so the regression gate cannot catch this. Recoverable by the user re-affirming, but it is a fidelity regression on very common phrasings now ON by default in `heartbit chat`.
suggested_fix: Match STUDY markers on word boundaries (split_whitespace + trim punctuation, as has_fr_conditional_volition already does); and treat an anchored text (has_concrete_anchor) ending in '?' as ambiguous (return None → L1/L2) rather than confident ANSWER, since 'can you/peux-tu + concrete file' is overwhelmingly a directive.

title: 256KB tool-result ingest cap silently bypassed when any repair/deps/escalation hint fires in the same turn (regression of 7de5df6 layer 2)
description: Commit 7de5df6 placed the ingest cap (`cap_last_tool_results`) immediately after `ctx.add_tool_results(results)`. Commit 4837ec9 (repair hints) later inserted `ctx.add_user_message(pending_hints.join(...))` BETWEEN the two. `cap_last_tool_results` (context.rs:186-193) only inspects `self.messages.last_mut()` and only truncates ToolResult blocks; when a hint fired, the last message is now the plain-text hint message, so the cap returns 0 and the actual fresh tool-results message (second-to-last) is NEVER capped. Hints fire exactly in the scenarios that produce giant outputs: (a) a rustc-failure-classified error result — e.g. an MCP build/exec tool (which, unlike bash's 30K self-cap, has no source-side cap) returning hundreds of KB of compile errors triggers the StaleApi/TypeMismatch hint on the very result that needed capping; (b) the deps hint fires on a Cargo.toml write co-batched with any other tool whose output is huge. This recreates incident 6a24e4bb's failure mode (one ~1MB fresh result -> 325K-token prompt -> API 400): the run then depends on layers 3/5 — and layer 5 only works if the provider's overflow phrasing matches `is_context_overflow`; otherwise the run dies. No test pins the cap+hint interaction (the four ingest_cap tests never fire a hint).
suggested_fix: Move the ingest-cap block to run immediately after `ctx.add_tool_results(results)` and BEFORE the `pending_hints` injection (restoring the 7de5df6 ordering); alternatively make `cap_last_tool_results` target the last message that actually contains ToolResult blocks. Add a regression test: oversized tool result + a firing deps/repair hint in the same turn must still be capped.

title: Reactive overflow recovery is single-shot: summarization fallback unreachable when deterministic truncation saves >0 bytes but the retry still overflows
description: On ContextOverflow, recovery first runs `truncate_oversized_tool_results`; if `saved > 0` it sets `compacted_last_turn = true` and retries. At the top of the retry turn, `can_compact = !compacted_last_turn` becomes false (runner.rs:933-934), so if the retry ALSO overflows — i.e. the overflow was dominated by aggregate bloat (assistant text, many sub-cap results, system prompt), not by the few oversized results that were truncated — the entire recovery branch is skipped and the run fails with the raw API error. The LLM-summarization fallback (designed exactly for "aggregate bloat") is only reachable when the deterministic pass saves ZERO bytes on the FIRST overflow. So the presence of a single >4KB tool result converts an otherwise recoverable aggregate-bloat overflow into a fatal RunFailed. Reachable with default config: `summarize_threshold` and `context_window_tokens` both default to None (runner.rs:549-550), so no proactive compaction runs and long sessions accumulate untruncated assistant text until the reactive path is the only defense.
suggested_fix: Track recovery stage instead of a boolean: on a second consecutive overflow where truncation already ran, fall through to the bounded `generate_summary` path (which cannot itself overflow) before declaring RunFailed. Keep a hard cap of e.g. 2 recovery attempts to preserve the anti-ping-pong property.

title: compress_tool_output sends the full unbounded tool output to the LLM — the compression call itself can overflow the window (same class as the generate_summary bug fixed in 7de5df6)
description: When `tool_output_compression_threshold` is set, every oversized fresh result is sent verbatim to the provider for compression BEFORE the ingest cap runs (runner.rs:2588-2600). Unlike `generate_summary`, which bounds its transcript via `bound_transcript` precisely so "the summary call must never itself overflow the window it is trying to rescue", `compress_tool_output` applies no input bound: a multi-MB result produces a guaranteed-failing 400 (wasted API call + latency) per oversized result per turn. The error path is fail-open (returns the original content, which the ingest cap then truncates), so the run survives, but the feature deterministically burns a failing LLM call exactly when it is supposed to help. Opt-in feature, hence low.
evidence:
runner.rs:3200-3210:
```rust
let request = CompletionRequest {
    system: "Compress the following tool output, ...".into(),
    messages: vec![Message::user(content.to_string())],
    tools: vec![],
    max_tokens: (self.max_tokens / 3).max(256),
    ...
};
```
No `bound_transcript`/byte budget is applied to `content`, in contrast to generate_summary (runner.rs:2887-2891) which computes `budget` from `context_window_tokens` and calls `bound_transcript`.
suggested_fix: Apply the same head+tail bound used by generate_summary before building the compression request, e.g. `let text = bound_transcript(content, budget)` with the window-derived budget, or skip compression and let the ingest cap handle anything above the window-clamped cap.

title: try_ripgrep buffers unbounded rg stdout in memory: --max-count is per-file, not a global cap, contradicting the in-code claim
description: The comment says `--max-count` "Cap[s] output at source to avoid buffering unbounded results", but ripgrep's `--max-count` limits matches PER FILE. `cmd.output().await` (grep.rs:196-199) collects the ENTIRE stdout into memory before the 100-line / 100KB caps are applied line-by-line. A permissive pattern (e.g. `.` or `e`) over a large source tree yields up to 101 match lines for EVERY file — potentially hundreds of MB buffered in the agent process before truncation. The model context stays protected by the post-hoc caps (the 6a24e4bb fix holds), but memory/latency are not source-bounded as the comment asserts. SKIP_DIRS pruning limits the worst offenders (target/, node_modules/), so impact is a degenerate-pattern memory spike rather than the original incident class.
evidence:
grep.rs:168-170:
```rust
// Cap output at source to avoid buffering unbounded results
.arg("--max-count")
.arg((MAX_MATCHES + 1).to_string());
```
grep.rs:196-199:
```rust
let output = cmd
    .output()
    .await
    .map_err(|e| Error::Agent(format!("rg not available: {e}")))?;
```
All of stdout is buffered before `for line in stdout.lines()` applies MAX_MATCHES/MAX_TOTAL_BYTES (grep.rs:208-219).
suggested_fix: Stream rg stdout (spawn + read lines incrementally, kill the child once MAX_MATCHES or MAX_TOTAL_BYTES is hit), or at minimum fix the comment and consider `--max-count` alongside `head`-style early termination via a piped reader.

title: New-file write through a symlinked intermediate directory escapes the workspace jail (and the protected-path guard) when no CorePathPolicy is configured
description: resolve_path's only filesystem-aware containment check is best-effort: `if let Ok(canonical) = normalized.canonicalize() && !canonical.starts_with(ws)`. std::fs::canonicalize requires the WHOLE path to exist, so for a write that CREATES a new file (final component absent) it returns Err and the check is skipped entirely. The only remaining guard is the lexical `normalized.starts_with(ws)` on a path produced by `crate::workspace::normalize_path` (workspace.rs:78), which resolves `.`/`..` but does NOT resolve symlinks. So if a symlink exists at an intermediate directory inside the workspace (e.g. `/repo/data -> /home/victim/.ssh`), a write to `data/authorized_keys` passes: lexical normalize = `/repo/data/authorized_keys` (starts_with /repo OK), canonicalize fails (file absent → skipped), is_protected runs on the LEXICAL path (mod.rs:279) so `~/.ssh` is not matched. WriteTool's no-policy branch (write.rs:158-169) then calls write_no_follow, whose `O_NOFOLLOW` only guards the trailing component (mod.rs:62-91, doc 98-110) — the kernel still follows the `/repo/data` symlink during path resolution, creating the file at `/home/victim/.ssh/authorized_keys` OUTSIDE the jail. The F-FS-1 remediation (write_beneath_root, per-component O_NOFOLLOW openat walk) is wired ONLY when path_policy is Some; the TUI (heartbit-tui/src/main.rs:366, path_policy never set) and the default CLI config (path_policy only built from a present `[sandbox]` section) leave it None. Read/Edit are not affected because they require the target to exist, so canonicalize succeeds and catches the escape; the gap is specifically NEW-file creation (drop authorized_keys / autostart / cron / a not-yet-existing shell rc outside the jail). Reachability without bash requires a pre-existing symlink in the workspace (an untrusted/cloned repo can ship one, since git preserves symlinks); via bash it is the accepted escape hatch, but this defeats the file-tool jail itself.
suggested_fix: In the no-path-policy write branch, canonicalize the target's PARENT directory (which exists) and verify the canonical parent still starts_with the workspace root before writing, OR route the workspace-only path through the same write_beneath_root per-component O_NOFOLLOW walk used for the policy case. Also evaluate is_protected against the canonicalized path, not the lexical one, so a symlink cannot lexically dodge protected_paths.

title: VERIFY_RESULT sentinel gate is forgeable by agent narration or untrusted tool output despite the 'can't spoof' comment
description: parse_latest_verify scans the ENTIRE rendered conversation (runner.rs:1790 calls it on `ctx.conversation_text()`, which includes assistant text and every tool result) and returns the LAST line matching `VERIFY_RESULT:` that contains `exit_code=`. The inline comment claims spoofing is prevented: 'a bare echo has no exit_code=, so it can't spoof a gate' — but only BARE echoes are filtered. A full-format line `VERIFY_RESULT: PASS exit_code=0 command=cargo test` is trivially reproducible by the working model in its final turn (making it the latest canonical sentinel), or can arrive inside untrusted tool output (a repo file that documents the verify format, a fetched web page, an MCP tool result). When `replan_on_verify_fail` is enabled (orchestrator.rs:620/1133/2897, codegen builder), the runner uses this parse to decide whether a RED verification should block natural completion (runner.rs:1787-1806); a forged PASS makes the gate skip the replan and let the agent finish on a genuinely failing build. The deterministic anti-over-report gate is thus bypassable by the very agent it is meant to police, and by injected content — providing false assurance. Impact is limited to control-flow (keep-working vs finish), not privilege, and the LLM goal-judge remains the stronger gate when a goal is set; hence low severity.
suggested_fix: Do not derive the gate verdict from free-text in the merged transcript. Key the deterministic gate on the VerifyOutcome returned directly by the VerifyCommandTool invocation (e.g. record the latest outcome in shared runner state when the tool executes) rather than re-parsing conversation_text, so neither agent narration nor untrusted tool output can introduce a sentinel line. Soften the comment's 'can't spoof a gate' claim.

title: chunk_message panics on multibyte UTF-8: byte-slice happens before the char-boundary fallback
description: chunk_message() slices `remaining[..max_len]` to look for a newline BEFORE the char-boundary fallback ever runs. The fallback closure only executes when rfind('\n') returns None — but the panicking slice is evaluated first. Whenever the text is longer than max_len and byte index max_len falls inside a multibyte UTF-8 character (emoji, accented letters), the slice panics with 'byte index is not a char boundary'. This is directly reachable in normal use: heartbit::channel re-exports this function (`pub use heartbit_core::channel::*;` in crates/heartbit/src/channel/mod.rs:10) and both the Discord bridge (crates/heartbit/src/channel/discord/mod.rs:75, `chunk_message(text, MAX_MESSAGE_LEN)`) and the Slack bridge (crates/heartbit/src/channel/slack/mod.rs:61) call it on LLM-generated reply text. Any agent reply over the platform limit (~2000 bytes for Discord) where the 2000th byte of a chunk splits a codepoint — e.g. a long French or emoji-bearing answer — panics the delivery path. The doc comment ('falls back to char boundaries') describes intent the code does not implement. A secondary edge in the same function: when split_at == 0 the code re-assigns `split_at = max_len.min(remaining.len())` (line 97), reintroducing the same non-boundary index even after the fallback computed a safe one.
suggested_fix: Compute the safe boundary first, then search within it: `let window_end = { let mut pos = max_len; while pos > 0 && !remaining.is_char_boundary(pos) { pos -= 1; } pos };` then `remaining[..window_end].rfind('\n')`, and in the `split_at == 0` fallback use `window_end.max(first-char-width)` (or `floor_char_boundary(remaining, max_len)` from tool::builtins) instead of raw `max_len`.

title: Intent router classify_l1 panics on LLM output where '}' precedes '{' — missing the end<=start guard its sibling parser has
description: The L1 fast-classifier parse extracts the 'outermost JSON object' from untrusted LLM text with `find('{')` / `rfind('}')` and slices `&body[start..=end]` without checking that end >= start. If the classifier model's reply contains a '}' before the first '{' and no '}' after it (e.g. body = "hmm} I cannot classify {oops" → start=23, end=3 → &body[23..4]), the slice panics with 'slice index starts at N but ends at M'. The identical parser in agent/intake.rs:202-204 (parse_gap_json) explicitly guards this exact case with `if end <= start { return None; }` — router.rs missed the guard. The router runs on every user request when wired (intent-mode router shipped 36a2d48, TUI+CLI wired), so a stray-brace classifier reply — or a prompt-injection payload crafted to steer the cheap classifier model's output — panics the thread driving the agent run instead of falling through to the safe default mode.
suggested_fix: Add the same guard as intake.rs before slicing: `if end <= start { return None; }` (or use the non-panicking `body.get(start..=end)?`).

title: WebSearch DuckDuckGo parser slices HTML at abs_marker-200, which can split a multibyte UTF-8 character
description: parse_duckduckgo_html() looks backwards for the href by slicing a fixed 200-byte window: `tag_start_region = abs_marker.saturating_sub(200)` then `&html[tag_start_region..abs_marker]`. abs_marker is a valid boundary (found via `find` of an ASCII marker), but abs_marker-200 is an arbitrary byte offset into third-party HTML. For the second and subsequent results, the 200 bytes preceding the `class="result__a"` marker include the previous result's snippet/title text — which for non-English queries (French, Japanese, emoji-bearing titles) is dense with multibyte characters, so the offset lands mid-codepoint with high probability and the slice panics. Mitigating factor: tool execution runs inside the runner's JoinSet, which converts the panic into a synthetic 'Tool execution panicked' tool-error result (agent/runner.rs:3444-3456), so with the default panic=unwind the run survives but the search silently fails with a misleading error; under panic=abort it kills the process. Every other parser in this file derives both slice ends from `find()` of ASCII patterns — this is the only backwards fixed-offset slice.
suggested_fix: Round the start up to a boundary before slicing: `let mut tag_start_region = abs_marker.saturating_sub(200); while !html.is_char_boundary(tag_start_region) { tag_start_region += 1; }` (a ceil counterpart to the existing builtins::floor_char_boundary), or use the non-panicking `html.get(tag_start_region..abs_marker).unwrap_or("")`.

title: Human-approval gate silently vanishes for delegated work: on_approval is not propagated to sub-agents, and Ask permission rules auto-allow without a callback
description: DelegateTaskTool (and FormSquadTool/SpawnAgentTool, built the same way) forward permission_rules, guardrails, and on_event to sub-agent runners, but never on_approval. In the runner, a rule that evaluates to Ask with no on_approval callback falls into the 'No callback -> allow' branch (runner.rs:2038-2041). The TUI wires default_permissions() with a wildcard Ask rule ('everything that can mutate the workspace asks the human', main.rs:912-939) and its on_approval enforces Plan mode by denying edit/write/patch/bash (main.rs:732-743) — but only on the entry agent. The moment the entry agent delegates (the user approves one innocuous-looking 'delegate_task' call in the modal), the sub-agent runs write/edit/patch/bash with zero human gate, in Normal AND Plan mode. Plan mode's read-only promise is therefore bypassable via delegation. Sub-agents in the TUI get dangerous_tools=true builtins, so this is a real mutation path. (Distinct from the accepted bash-jail risk: this is the approval/HITL gate, not the path jail.)
suggested_fix: Propagate the orchestrator's on_approval Arc to sub-agent runners in DelegateTaskTool/FormSquadTool/SpawnAgentTool (mirroring the F-AGENT-2 guardrail-propagation fix), or change the runner's no-callback Ask fallback to Deny when permission rules are present. At minimum, default the forwarded ruleset's wildcard Ask to Deny for sub-agents.

title: VerifyCommandTool spawns its child without kill_on_drop/process-group: a mid-tool interrupt (or timeout) orphans a running cargo build/test
description: The runner's tool-batch interrupt contract (runner.rs:2530-2531) assumes 'JoinSet drop kills any in-flight subprocess via kill_on_drop'. BashTool honours this (kill_on_drop + process_group(0) + ProcessGroupKiller, bash.rs:255-301), but VerifyCommandTool spawns bash WITHOUT kill_on_drop and without a process group. When the user hits Esc mid-verify in the TUI (/verify is wired at main.rs:589), the select! drops the batch future, the JoinSet aborts the task at its await, and the tokio Child is dropped — which does NOT kill the process. A heavy `cargo test`/`cargo build` keeps running detached, eating CPU and holding the target/ build lock (the next verify or the user's own build then stalls on the lock). The timeout path has the same leak, and its comment claims it 'mirrors BashTool' — stale: BashTool was since fixed to tear down the whole group.
evidence: verify.rs:208-215: `let child = tokio::process::Command::new("bash").arg("-c").arg(command).current_dir(&self.workspace)...spawn();` — no `.kill_on_drop(true)`, no `process_group(0)`. verify.rs:257-259: `// Known limitation (mirrors BashTool): the timed-out child is not killed...` (BashTool no longer has this limitation). runner.rs:2530-2531: `// result for EVERY allowed call ... drop the batch future (its JoinSet drop kills any in-flight subprocess via kill_on_drop)`.
suggested_fix: Mirror BashTool: add .kill_on_drop(true), spawn in its own process group via cmd.as_std_mut().process_group(0), and arm a ProcessGroupKiller (disarmed on clean exit) so both the timeout branch and an interrupt-driven future drop tear the whole tree down.

title: TUI RespawnAgent while a turn is in flight produces two concurrently-running engines on the same workspace
description: /model, /model advisor, and advisor-clear push Effect::RespawnAgent unconditionally (app.rs:1394-1428, no gate on self.running). RespawnAgent swaps the input channel and sets agent_started=false, but the old agent thread only exits when it next reaches on_input — i.e. at the END of its current turn, which can be minutes of tool calls/delegations. If the user sends the next message before that (submit() is not gated on running either, app.rs:1104-1145), Effect::SendInput spawns a brand-new engine (epoch+1) while the old one is still executing: two engines stream interleaved StreamDelta/events into the same ui_tx (the exact crisscross fa20786 eliminated for sub-agents), both can run mutating tools concurrently in the same cwd, the old engine's text-only LlmDone flips app.running=false while the new engine is mid-work, and both share the same InterruptHandle so Esc hits both. The stale AgentExited is correctly ignored by the epoch check, but nothing prevents the overlap window itself.
evidence: main.rs:1194-1207: `Effect::RespawnAgent => { ... let (ntx, nrx) = tokio::sync::mpsc::unbounded_channel::<String>(); input_tx = ntx; input_rx = Arc::new(Mutex::new(nrx)); agent_started = false; }` and main.rs:1177-1191: `if !agent_started { agent_epoch += 1; agent_started = spawn_agent(..., "respawn"); } let _ = input_tx.send(text);` — the old thread is still inside `engine.run` (main.rs:1069-1072) until its turn ends. app.rs:1394-1404: `fn set_model(&mut self, model: String) { ... self.effects.push(Effect::RespawnAgent); ... }` with no `self.running` gate.
suggested_fix: On RespawnAgent while agent_started && app.running, also fire the InterruptHandle (forcing the old engine to its on_input boundary quickly) and/or defer the channel swap until the matching AgentExited(epoch) arrives; alternatively refuse /model mid-run like /learn does (app.rs:1247).

title: Esc race at turn boundary leaves the interrupt token cancelled while idle; the next user message is instantly self-interrupted
description: Effect::Interrupt is gated on app.running, but running is UI-derived: between the agent finishing its turn (entering the on_input await) and the UI processing the LlmDone message, an Esc still fires interrupt.interrupt(). Nothing rearms the token while the runner idles in on_input — rearm only happens inside the LLM/tool races (runner.rs:1141). The next user message then starts a turn whose biased select sees the already-cancelled token and immediately synthesizes '[interrupted by user]' (runner.rs:1135-1146), ending the turn without doing any work; the user must resend. Self-healing (the race rearms the token) and the window is one event-loop iteration, but it is a real interrupt-vs-idle race in the shared InterruptHandle design.
evidence: app.rs:1684-1690: `// Esc interrupts a running turn; when idle it just clears the composer.\n ... if self.running {` (interrupt fires). interrupt.rs:59-63: `/// Swap in a fresh token, arming the handle for the next turn. Called by the runner right after it has handled an interrupt.` — no rearm on the idle path; runner.rs:1135-1145 races the next turn's LLM call against the stale-cancelled token.
suggested_fix: Rearm the handle when the runner parks on on_input (or check-and-rearm a token that was cancelled before the turn's first LLM call), so an interrupt that lands while idle is a no-op for the next message.

title: Runtime goal continuation budget never re-arms on a new user request — second `set_goal` in a chat session can get ZERO continuations
description: `goal_continuations_used` is declared once before the chat loop (line 848) and is never reset when `on_input` delivers a new user request. The on_input re-arm block (lines 1904-1923) resets a dozen per-request gates (`nudge_tool_calls`, `request_tool_calls`, `plan_gate_fired`, etc.) under the comment 'New user request: all per-request gates re-arm.' — but NOT `goal_continuations_used`. Consequence on the live entry-agent path (orchestrator wires `goal_slot` + `SetGoalTool`, TUI uses it): if the goal for request 1 consumes its continuation budget (default 8) before auto-clearing, a NEW goal installed via `set_goal` on request 2 is checked against the already-spent counter — `goal_continuations_used < goal.max_continuations()` is immediately false, so the judge runs once, the verdict's continuation is discarded, `last_goal_met = Some(false)` and the goal silently clears with zero continuations granted. Even a partially-spent budget bleeds into every later goal. This violates the documented per-GoalCondition contract ('bounded by the goal's max_continuations', builder.rs:533) and re-creates exactly the 'inert plumbing' class of bug commit 1373234 fixed — the completion loop goes dead for second+ requests. No test covers two goals across two chat requests: `goal_gates_before_next_input_in_chat_mode` (runner.rs:4705) uses ONE goal that settles before the follow-up, and `entry_agent_set_goal_tool_installs_runtime_goal` (orchestrator.rs:5251) is single-request.
evidence:
runner.rs:848  `let mut goal_continuations_used: u32 = 0;`  (loop-lifetime, not request-lifetime)
runner.rs:1834-1835  `} else if goal_continuations_used < goal.max_continuations() {\n    goal_continuations_used += 1;`
runner.rs:1865 + 1905-1923 (the re-arm block):  `// New user request: all per-request gates re-arm.` … `nudge_tool_calls = 0; nudge_delegated = false; nudge_sent = false; … escalation_fired = false;` — `goal_continuations_used` is absent.
suggested_fix: Reset `goal_continuations_used = 0;` (and re-arm per request) in the on_input block at runner.rs:1904-1923. Add a regression test: chat-mode runner with `goal_slot` + `SetGoalTool`; request 1 installs a goal with `with_max_continuations(1)` and exhausts it (judge always NO); on_input delivers request 2 which installs a second goal; judge says NO once then YES — assert the continuation message IS injected for goal 2 (budget re-armed) and `goal_met == Some(true)`.

title: Verify-fail replan budget (MAX_VERIFY_REPLANS) is session-cumulative — gate goes permanently dead mid-session, untested across requests
description: Same missing re-arm as the goal budget: `verify_replans_used` (line 854, cap `MAX_VERIFY_REPLANS = 8`) is never reset in the on_input re-arm block. The entry-agent path auto-enables this gate (orchestrator.rs:2897-2898 `runner_builder.replan_on_verify_fail(true)`), and since the stop-gate order fix (1373234) the gate now fires on EVERY natural stop in a long-lived TUI chat session. A permanently-red verify on an early request consumes the whole budget; on a later, unrelated request a genuinely RED `VERIFY_RESULT: FAIL` no longer blocks completion — the agent finishes on red with no replan nudge, silently. The only tests (`replan_on_verify_fail_blocks_completion_but_is_bounded`, runner.rs:3733, and `no_replan_when_gate_disabled`) are single-request, so the cross-request decay is invisible to the suite.
suggested_fix: Reset `verify_replans_used = 0;` in the on_input re-arm block (it is a per-request gate like the others; the per-loop boundedness is preserved). Add a chat-mode test: request 1 exhausts the 8 replans on a red verify, request 2 runs a fresh red verify — assert the replan nudge fires again on request 2.

title: ScopeGuard vs relative file paths: live combination (absolute roots from set_scope + workspace-relative file_path) is untested and false-denies in-scope writes
description: ScopeGuard compares the RAW tool-call `file_path` lexically against the roots, with the documented rule 'Relative roots only match relative paths and vice versa' (scope_guard.rs:27). But on the live path the two sides come in different flavors: `SetScopeTool` deliberately absolutizes relative roots against the workspace (set_scope.rs:99-103, live finding 6a25d21b), while the file tools ACCEPT workspace-relative `file_path` (pinned by `resolve_path_relative_with_workspace`, builtins/mod.rs:694). So once a scope is declared (always absolute roots in the TUI), every edit/write the model issues with a relative path — including ones squarely INSIDE the declared scratch root — is denied with 'outside the current task scope'. Every existing test in scope_guard.rs (lines 164+) and set_scope.rs uses same-flavor paths on both sides (absolute/absolute or relative root tests with relative targets), so the real mixed-flavor code path shipped with zero coverage. This degrades exactly the live workflows (scratch-dir builds) the feature was shipped to fix; recovery requires the model to guess it must retry with an absolute path.
evidence:
scope_guard.rs:120-128  `let target = normalize_path(&path); … let in_scope = roots.iter().any(|root| target.starts_with(root));` — a relative `target` can never `starts_with` an absolute root.
scope_guard.rs:27  `//! Relative roots only match relative paths and vice versa.`
set_scope.rs:99-103  `let p = PathBuf::from(s); match (&self.workspace, p.is_relative()) { (Some(ws), true) => ws.join(p), _ => p, }` — roots are stored ABSOLUTE.
builtins/mod.rs:694  `fn resolve_path_relative_with_workspace()` — file tools accept relative `file_path` and resolve it against the workspace.
suggested_fix: Give ScopeGuard the workspace root (mirror SetScopeTool::with_workspace) and resolve a relative target against it in `decide()` before the `starts_with` check. Add the missing test: roots = ["/repo/scratch-x"], call `write` with `file_path: "scratch-x/app.py"` → must be Allow (and `file_path: "src/main.rs"` → Deny).

title: Stop-gate order fix is only half-pinned: no regression test that the verify-replan gate runs before on_input in chat mode
description: Commit 1373234 fixed BOTH gates that sat after the blocking `on_input().await` ('replan + goal gates sat AFTER the blocking on_input()'). The regression test `goal_gates_before_next_input_in_chat_mode` (runner.rs:4705) pins only the GOAL gate's position. The replan gate (runner.rs:1787-1806) is a separate block; a refactor that moves it back after the input await — re-introducing the exact 'inert mid-session, fires only at session end' bug for the no-goal path — passes the entire suite, because both existing replan tests (runner.rs:3733, 3760) run WITHOUT on_input (non-chat mode). This is the one bug class that has already shipped once in this code.
evidence:
runner.rs:1787-1791  `if self.replan_on_verify_fail && verify_replans_used < MAX_VERIFY_REPLANS && let Some(outcome) = crate::codegen::parse_latest_verify(…) && !outcome.passed` — sits before the `on_input` await at 1861 with no test pinning that ordering.
runner.rs:3733  `async fn replan_on_verify_fail_blocks_completion_but_is_bounded()` — builds the runner with no `.on_input(...)` (non-chat), as does `no_replan_when_gate_disabled` (3760).
suggested_fix: Add `replan_gates_before_next_input_in_chat_mode`: runner with `.replan_on_verify_fail(true)`, a red-verify tool, and an `on_input` that yields one follow-up; assert the 'Verification is RED' corrective message appears in the request BEFORE the follow-up user message (mirror the structure of goal_gates_before_next_input_in_chat_mode).

title: AgentRunnerBuilder goal()+goal_slot() seeding-precedence branch has zero coverage — documented contract 'slot wins' is unpinned
description: The public builder contract (builder.rs:541-544 rustdoc: 'Takes precedence over Self::goal as the storage (a goal() value seeds the slot only if the slot is empty)') is implemented at build() lines 882-896, but no test anywhere constructs a runner with BOTH `.goal(...)` and `.goal_slot(...)` set. The orchestrator entry path seeds the slot directly (`Arc::new(std::sync::RwLock::new(self.entry_goal.take()))`, orchestrator.rs:2919-2920) and never calls `.goal()`, so the seed-only-if-empty branch is dead in every test run. The project mandates every public function have at least one test; `goal_slot()` is public API consumable by library users, and a regression flipping the precedence (seed overwriting an installed runtime goal) would be invisible to the suite.
evidence: builder.rs:882-896  `goal: match self.goal_slot { Some(slot) => { // Seed the shared slot from goal() only when empty — a\n// goal already installed in the slot wins.\nif let Some(seed) = self.goal { … if g.is_none() { *g = Some(seed); } } slot } None => … }` — grep shows `goal_slot` appears in runner.rs tests zero times; orchestrator tests only use entry_goal/entry_goal_judge which bypass `.goal()`.
suggested_fix: Two unit tests on the builder: (1) slot pre-loaded with goal A + `.goal(B)` → built runner's slot still holds A; (2) empty slot + `.goal(B)` → slot holds B after build.

title: DelegationNudge per-request re-arm ('resets at on_input') is shipped behavior with no test
description: Commit 47007b0's documented contract is 'after N direct tool calls on ONE user request (resets at on_input)'. The reset lives at runner.rs:1905-1907 (`nudge_tool_calls = 0; nudge_delegated = false; nudge_sent = false;`), but all four nudge tests (`delegation_nudge_fires_once_after_threshold` 5785, `delegation_nudge_suppressed_when_delegation_used` 5821, `delegation_nudge_absent_by_default` 5855, `entry_agent_auto_wires_delegation_nudge` orchestrator.rs:5303) are single-request. Deleting the three reset lines passes the whole suite, silently turning the nudge into once-per-session — and since the live finding behind the feature is that delegation NEVER fires organically, a once-per-session nudge materially weakens the only deterministic lever, in the long-lived TUI sessions where it matters most. The nudge is itself flagged 'not yet live-validated', so tests are its only safety net.
evidence:
runner.rs:1905-1907 (inside the on_input block):  `nudge_tool_calls = 0;\nnudge_delegated = false;\nnudge_sent = false;`
runner.rs:5785-5818  `delegation_nudge_fires_once_after_threshold` — single `execute("substantive task")`, no `.on_input(...)`; same for the other three nudge tests.
suggested_fix: Add `delegation_nudge_rearms_on_new_request`: nudge with `after_tool_calls: 2`, on_input yields one follow-up; the model makes 2 solo calls per request — assert the '[delegation check]' message appears twice (once per request), and that delegating during request 1 does not suppress the request-2 nudge.

title: Tag push publishes heartbit-core to crates.io with zero test gate; CI never runs on tags
description: The publish-crate job added in f3734f8 depends only on `needs: build`, and the `build` job runs nothing but `cargo build --release -p heartbit-cli` (a compile of the CLI, not even heartbit-core's own tests or clippy). Meanwhile ci.yml triggers only on `push: branches: [main]` and `pull_request` — NOT on tag pushes. So a `v*` tag pushed from ANY commit (including one that never went through CI, e.g. a local commit pushed only via the tag) publishes heartbit-core to crates.io completely untested once CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN is set. crates.io versions are immutable (yank-only). Two aggravating details: (a) the version is read from the checked-out root Cargo.toml (`VER=$(grep -m1 '^version' Cargo.toml ...)`), with no check that it matches the tag name — tagging v2026.608.1 without bumping Cargo.toml makes the idempotency guard see 2026.607.1 already on crates.io and silently `exit 0`, producing a green 'release' that published nothing; (b) even the branch CI gate is weaker than the documented one: `cargo test --workspace --lib` (no integration/doc tests) and no `--exclude mini-crm` despite CLAUDE.md/Cargo.toml documenting mini-crm as excluded-from-gate WIP.
evidence:
release.yml:56-58: `publish-crate:
  name: Publish heartbit-core to crates.io
  needs: build` — and the build job's only check is line 46: `run: cargo build --release -p heartbit-cli --target ${{ matrix.target }}`. release.yml:84-91: `VER=$(grep -m1 '^version' Cargo.toml | sed -E 's/.*"(.*)".*/\1/')` ... `if curl -s "https://index.crates.io/he/ar/heartbit-core" | grep -q ""vers":"$VER""; then ... exit 0 ... fi; cargo publish -p heartbit-core`. ci.yml:3-6: `on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:` (no tags), ci.yml:37: `run: cargo test --workspace --lib`.
suggested_fix: Add a test job to release.yml (fmt + clippy -D warnings + the full documented gate with --exclude mini-crm) and make publish-crate `needs: [build, test]`. Also assert tag↔version consistency before publishing: fail (don't exit 0) when `v$VER` != `$GITHUB_REF_NAME`, keeping the existing already-published skip only for re-runs of the same tag.

title: Shipped example config sets [orchestrator].system_prompt — a key that does not exist; the entire pipeline prompt is silently dropped
description: configs/twitter-content-gen.toml (committed example, header says `Run: cargo run -- run -c configs/twitter-content-gen.toml ...`) puts its core artifact — the 5-step research→writers→judge→image→publish pipeline instructions — under `[orchestrator] system_prompt = """..."""`. But `OrchestratorConfig` (crates/heartbit-core/src/config/agent.rs:52-125) has no `system_prompt` field, the struct is not `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`, and `HeartbitConfig::validate()` has no unknown-key check, so the key deserializes to nothing with no warning. The CLI orchestrator build path (heartbit-cli/src/main.rs:1650+) never wires any orchestrator system prompt from config either. Net effect: the example runs as a generic orchestrator with default instructions; the documented EXACT-order pipeline, the 'pass FULL context' rule, and the stop-on-failure rule never reach the model. Anyone using this shipped config as a reference will write dead config keys.
evidence:
configs/twitter-content-gen.toml:13-17: `[orchestrator]
max_turns = 15
dispatch_mode = "sequential"
routing = "always_orchestrate"
system_prompt = """You are a social media content pipeline orchestrator for X/Twitter..."""`. config/agent.rs:51-52: `#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
pub struct OrchestratorConfig {` — fields are max_turns, max_tokens, context_strategy, ..., spawn, max_tokens_in_flight_per_tenant; no system_prompt and no deny_unknown_fields (the only config struct with `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` is ProviderCircuitConfig, config/provider.rs:103). grep of heartbit-cli/src/main.rs shows no orchestrator system-prompt wiring (system_prompt is only read per-agent, e.g. main.rs:1337-1344).
suggested_fix: Either add a real `system_prompt: Option<String>` to OrchestratorConfig and wire it into Orchestrator::builder in the CLI, or move the pipeline instructions in the example into the task/an entry agent and delete the dead key. Longer term, consider deny_unknown_fields (or a warn-on-unknown pass) on config structs so typo'd/removed keys fail loudly.

title: Uncommitted Cargo.toml adds two untracked stub crates as workspace members — a partial commit bricks every fresh clone, and the stubs pollute the quality gate
description: The working tree has a modified (uncommitted) root Cargo.toml that appends `crates/heartbit-crm-core` and `crates/heartbit-crm-cli` to workspace members, plus a matching uncommitted Cargo.lock hunk — while both crate directories are UNTRACKED (`?? crates/heartbit-crm-cli/`, `?? crates/heartbit-crm-core/`). If Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock get committed without `git add`-ing the crate dirs (easy with `git commit -am` or a selective commit touching workspace deps), every fresh clone and CI run fails immediately with 'failed to load manifest for workspace member'. The crates themselves are pure cargo-new boilerplate (lib.rs: `add(left, right)` with the `it_works` test; main.rs: `println!("Hello, world!")`) carrying `version.workspace = true` = 2026.607.1, and since the documented gate only excludes mini-crm, they are now inside `cargo test/clippy --workspace --exclude mini-crm`, inflating gate numbers with placeholder code. There are also stray EMPTY duplicate dirs at repo root (/heartbit-crm-core/src, /heartbit-crm-cli/src — a cargo-new misfire; invisible to git but confusing clutter).
evidence:
git diff Cargo.toml: `-members = [... "mini-crm"]
+members = [... "mini-crm", "crates/heartbit-crm-core", "crates/heartbit-crm-cli"]` with `?? crates/heartbit-crm-cli/` and `?? crates/heartbit-crm-core/` in git status. crates/heartbit-crm-core/src/lib.rs: `pub fn add(left: u64, right: u64) -> u64 { left + right }`; crates/heartbit-crm-cli/src/main.rs: `fn main() { println!("Hello, world!"); }`. git diff Cargo.lock: `+[[package]]
+name = "heartbit-crm-cli"
+version = "2026.607.1"
+
+[[package]]
+name = "heartbit-crm-core"
+version = "2026.607.1"`.
suggested_fix: Either commit the stub crates together with Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock in one atomic commit (and decide whether they belong in the gate), or revert the member additions and develop the CRM crates outside the workspace until they have real content. Remove the empty root-level heartbit-crm-core/ and heartbit-crm-cli/ dirs.

title: CHANGELOG stale again: 8 commits (5 changing heartbit-core behavior) shipped after the v2026.607.1 tag with no version bump and no [Unreleased] section
description: Tag v2026.607.1 resolves to 4f06385, and 8 commits have landed since — f3734f8 (release CI), bfe4782 (TUI respawn), a2ff809 (gate observability + hard escalation), 9ecd8d6 (bash cwd visibility, doom-loop hard-stop), 699d01b (filesystem-boundary prompt), fa20786 (sub-agent streaming contract), 05ea2f6 (parallel fan-out refuse-once nudge), 5c7f319 (scratch-dir guidance + set_scope rework). Five of these materially change heartbit-core runtime behavior (orchestrator.rs, runner.rs, set_scope.rs, bash.rs, builder.rs), yet the workspace version is still 2026.607.1 (immutable — already tagged, the exact condition the 2026-06-07 release audit flagged as the sole blocker last cycle) and CHANGELOG.md has no entry/[Unreleased] section for them: its newest heading is `## [2026.607.1] - 2026-06-07`. Additionally, the Notes block at line 76 says 'The `[Unreleased]` section below is the detail of the heartbit-ghost P1.1 X-tool family...' but no `## [Unreleased]` heading exists anywhere in the file (the next heading is `## [2026.507.4]` at line 79) — the prose references a section that was renamed away.
evidence: `git rev-parse v2026.607.1^{commit}` = 4f063859...; `git log v2026.607.1..HEAD --oneline | wc -l` = 8; Cargo.toml:11 `version = "2026.607.1"`; `grep -n "^## " CHANGELOG.md` shows the first heading is line 7 `## [2026.607.1] - 2026-06-07` (no [Unreleased]); CHANGELOG.md:76 `- The \`[Unreleased]\` section below is the detail of the heartbit-ghost P1.1 X-tool family`.
suggested_fix: Add an `## [Unreleased]` section covering f3734f8..5c7f319 now (and fix or delete the line-76 Notes reference); bump the workspace version before the next tag so the release workflow's idempotency guard cannot silently no-op.

title: Untracked scratch projects at repo root are not gitignored (wget-log escapes the *.log pattern)
description: git status shows persistent untracked dirs/files at the repo root that no .gitignore rule covers: crm-project/ (contains its own Cargo.toml + src/ + data/ — a nested cargo package inside the repo), crm_project/ (src/, static/, templates/, tests/), plate_solving_research/, plate_solving_rust/, scratch-rpg-game/, and wget-log. The .gitignore only ignores the literal `scratch/` dir and `*.log` — and `wget-log` does NOT match `*.log` (no `.log` suffix). These are agent-session scratch outputs that the project's own guidance says belong in the gitignored ./scratch dir (commit 5c7f319). Risk: a `git add -A` / `git commit -a`-style commit sweeps multi-file scratch projects (including crm-project's data/ payload) into the repo; the permanent `??` noise also masks genuinely new files in status output.
evidence:
git status --porcelain: `?? crm-project/
?? plate_solving_research/
?? plate_solving_rust/
?? scratch-rpg-game/
?? wget-log`. .gitignore:9 `*.log` (does not match `wget-log`) and .gitignore:55-56 `# Agent scratch/temporary work...
scratch/` (covers only ./scratch). crm-project/ contains `Cargo.toml`, `data/`, `src/` (ls output).
suggested_fix: Move these into the already-ignored ./scratch/ dir (per the project's own 5c7f319 convention), or add explicit ignore entries (`crm-project/`, `crm_project/`, `plate_solving_*/`, `scratch-rpg-game/`, `wget-log*`); delete wget-log.

title: Real durability bugfix (flush after write in JsonlQuoteSeenStore) sitting uncommitted in the working tree
description: The working tree contains an uncommitted, unstaged 4-line fix in heartbit-ghost's JsonlQuoteSeenStore: an explicit `file.flush().await?` after `write_all`, with a comment explaining that without it the tokio::fs write can still be in-flight on the blocking pool when the file is dropped, so readers and a fast process exit can miss the seen-line (i.e., the dedupe store can lose records → duplicate quote posts). This is a genuine reliability fix that is at risk of being lost to a stash/checkout, and it is silently absent from any commit/changelog — the deployed/tagged code still has the bug it fixes.
evidence:
git diff crates/heartbit-ghost/src/quote/sources.rs: `             file.write_all(line.as_bytes()).await?;
+            // tokio::fs::File buffers internally: without an explicit flush the
+            // write may still be in-flight on the blocking pool when the file
+            // is dropped — readers (and a fast process exit) can miss the line.
+            file.flush().await?;`
suggested_fix: Commit the fix (with a test if the TDD gate requires one) so it isn't lost and lands in the next release; until committed, the tagged code still has the lost-write window.

title: Sub-agent LlmResponse/RunCompleted/RunFailed leak into the UI Msg plane unattributed — running flag flips mid-run, roster permanently mis-settles, /learn commits early, false terminal failure + emergency brief
description: Commit a28fbd9 kept RECIPE-internal events trace-only, but the DELEGATION plane was never filtered: heartbit-core forwards the full on_event to every sub-agent (orchestrator.rs:603-606 'Forward on_event so sub-agent events are visible' and the FormSquadTool path at 1121-1124), and Msg::from_event maps LlmResponse, RunCompleted and RunFailed while DISCARDING the agent field. The TUI reducer then treats sub-agent lifecycle events as the entry agent's. Consequences, all reachable on any delegation (a shipped, nudged behavior — 47007b0): (1) a sub-agent's final text-only LlmResponse (tool_call_count==0, guaranteed at every sub-agent completion) sets running=false mid-run — Esc in that window clears the composer instead of interrupting (app.rs:1685-1691), the tick/spinner freezes (main.rs:1161 gate), and autosave churns; (2) the same arm calls agents_settle() which marks ALL Working roster rows Done, and agent_set_working (app.rs:628-635) deliberately never resurrects Done rows — so after the FIRST parallel sibling finishes, the roster permanently shows still-working siblings as Done for the rest of the turn (corrupts the dispatch-gated roster feature); (3) if learning=Some (a /learn turn that delegates — plausible given the 8-call DelegationNudge), the digest is consumed and Effect::CommitLessons fires BEFORE the entry agent rewrote the staged file → 'lessons unchanged' and the real rewrite is silently never committed; (4) a sub-agent RunFailed (e.g. its max_turns=60 exceeded, runner.rs:924-929 — routine under doom loops) maps to Msg::RunFailed → the reducer declares the whole run failed, clears learning, pushes 'run failed: Max turns (60) exceeded' and writes an EMERGENCY HANDOFF BRIEF (app.rs:895-909) while the orchestrator continues normally (delegate_task just returns the error as a tool result); (5) sub-agent LlmResponse usage overwrites context_tokens, so the context-fill bar shows the sub-agent's window fill, not the entry agent's.
evidence:
msg.rs:131-141 — `AgentEvent::LlmResponse { usage, tool_call_count, time_to_first_token_ms, .. } => Some(Msg::LlmDone { usage, had_tool_calls: tool_call_count > 0, ttft_ms: ... })` (agent field dropped); msg.rs:185-186 — `AgentEvent::RunCompleted { .. } => Some(Msg::RunCompleted), AgentEvent::RunFailed { error, .. } => Some(Msg::RunFailed(error))`. app.rs:793-800 — `if !had_tool_calls { self.running = false; self.agents_settle(); if let Some(digest) = self.learning.take() { self.effects.push(Effect::CommitLessons(digest)); } }`. app.rs:895-905 — `Msg::RunFailed(error) => { ... self.running = false; self.learning = None; ... self.effects.push(Effect::EmergencyHandoff(error));`. Core forwarding: heartbit-core/src/agent/orchestrator.rs:603-605 — `// Forward on_event so sub-agent events are visible
if let Some(ref on_event) = on_event { builder = builder.on_event(on_event.clone()); }`; sub-agent terminal events: heartbit-core/src/agent/runner.rs:924-928 — `self.emit(AgentEvent::RunFailed { agent: self.name.clone(), error: format!("Max turns ({}) exceeded", ...), ... })`.
suggested_fix: Thread the agent name through Msg::LlmDone/RunCompleted/RunFailed and gate the run-state transitions (running, learning commit, agents_settle, EmergencyHandoff) on the ENTRY agent's name; map sub-agent LlmResponse/RunCompleted/RunFailed to roster-only updates (the SubAgentCompleted event already does the per-row finish). Alternatively wrap the on_event forwarded to sub-agents in core with an attributing filter, mirroring the on_text contract from fa20786.

title: /model (and /model advisor) mid-run spawns a second concurrent engine — two agents share the workspace/UI; stale AgentExited then flips running=false during the new run
description: set_model/set_frontier_model/clear_frontier_model push Effect::RespawnAgent with no `running` gate. The RespawnAgent handler only swaps the input channel; the OLD engine keeps executing its in-flight turn (the closed channel is observed only at the next on_input await, which can be minutes away mid-turn). Because the notice says 'active on your next message', the natural next step — sending a message — hits `if !agent_started { spawn_agent(...) }` and starts a SECOND engine while the first is still running: both stream into the same `app.active` buffer (the exact crisscross bug class fa20786 fixed for sub-agents), both execute tools concurrently in the same workspace, MCP servers are spawned twice, and both can pop approval modals. Additionally, when the old thread finally exits, run_ui's epoch guard only protects `agent_started`, but `app.update(Msg::AgentExited(stale_epoch))` still runs the reducer arm — `Msg::AgentExited(_)` ignores the epoch — setting running=false and clearing `learning` in the middle of the NEW engine's run.
evidence: app.rs:1394-1404 — `fn set_model(&mut self, model: String) { self.model = model.clone(); self.effects.push(Effect::SaveModel(model.clone())); self.effects.push(Effect::RespawnAgent); ... }` (no running check). main.rs:1194-1207 — `Effect::RespawnAgent => { ... let (ntx, nrx) = tokio::sync::mpsc::unbounded_channel::<String>(); input_tx = ntx; input_rx = Arc::new(Mutex::new(nrx)); agent_started = false; }` (old engine not interrupted). main.rs:1177-1192 — `if !agent_started { agent_epoch += 1; agent_started = spawn_agent(...); } let _ = input_tx.send(text);`. app.rs:887-894 — `Msg::AgentExited(_) => { self.finalize_active(); self.running = false; ... self.learning = None; }` (epoch unchecked in the reducer).
suggested_fix: In the RespawnAgent handler, call interrupt.interrupt() (or defer the respawn until AgentExited for the current epoch arrives) so only one engine is ever live; carry the epoch into the reducer (e.g. Msg::AgentExited{epoch, current} or filter the Msg at the edge) so a stale exit is a no-op in app.update too.

title: /clear and /resume (SessionLoaded) leave tool_index stale — an in-flight ToolCompleted can overwrite the wrong Cell::Tool in the replaced transcript
description: tool_index maps in-flight tool_call_id → index into `history`. The `/clear` slash handler clears history/todos/agents but NOT tool_index, and Msg::SessionLoaded replaces history wholesale without clearing it either. Both are reachable while a run is in flight (slash commands are not gated on running). When the in-flight tool completes, `history.get_mut(idx)` is matched against `Cell::Tool` — if the regrown (after /clear) or resumed transcript happens to have a Tool cell at that index, its status/output/duration are overwritten with another tool's result (corrupted transcript, and the corrupted state is then auto-saved). When the index is out of bounds it silently no-ops, which is benign.
evidence: app.rs:1183-1190 — `"clear" | "new" => { self.history.clear(); self.todos.clear(); self.agents.clear(); self.follow = true; ... }` (tool_index untouched); app.rs:951-956 — `Msg::SessionLoaded(history) => { self.history = history; ... }` (tool_index untouched); app.rs:859-875 — `if let Some(&idx) = self.tool_index.get(&id) && let Some(Cell::Tool { status, output: out, duration_ms: dur, .. }) = self.history.get_mut(idx) { *status = ...; *out = Some(output); ... }`.
suggested_fix: Clear `self.tool_index` (and `self.active`/`self.active_reasoning` for SessionLoaded) whenever `history` is cleared or replaced.

title: Agent-thread panic never sends AgentExited — running stuck true, agent_started never resets, all subsequent messages silently dropped
description: The agent thread's exit signal `done_tx.send(Msg::AgentExited(epoch))` lives at the END of the rt.block_on async block. If anything in the thread panics (the `.expect("agent runtime")` on runtime build, or any panic inside build_engine/the runner/a dependency), the thread unwinds and the AgentExited message is never sent: `agent_started` stays true forever, so Effect::SendInput never respawns, and `let _ = input_tx.send(text)` ignores the send error from the dead receiver — every subsequent user message vanishes silently while submit() re-sets running=true (spinner forever; Esc 'interrupts' nothing). The session is permanently wedged with no visible diagnosis (stderr is the alt-screen). This is the exact 'flags set but never cleared after agent thread panic' wedge.
evidence: main.rs:1038-1043 — `std::thread::spawn(move || { let rt = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread().worker_threads(2).enable_all().build().expect("agent runtime"); rt.block_on(async move { ... ` and main.rs:1079-1081 — `// Signal this thread's exit ...\n let _ = done_tx.send(Msg::AgentExited(epoch));` (only reached on normal return); main.rs:1192 — `let _ = input_tx.send(text);` (send-to-dead-channel error discarded).
suggested_fix: Send AgentExited from a drop guard (struct holding done_tx+epoch with a Drop impl declared before block_on), or wrap the body in catch_unwind; additionally surface `input_tx.send` failure as a Cell::Notice and reset agent_started so the next message respawns.

title: Wrapped-row count truncated to u16 — transcript follow/scroll breaks past 65,535 visual rows in a long session
description: Paragraph::line_count returns usize; the `as u16` cast wraps modulo 65,536. Once a long session's transcript exceeds 65,535 post-wrap visual rows (an all-day agent run with verbose tool output at narrow widths), `total` wraps to a small number, max_off collapses, and follow mode pins the view near the TOP of the transcript — the latest output becomes unreachable by scrolling (everything below the wrapped offset is unviewable), which reads as transcript loss. ratatui's scroll offset is inherently u16, so the cap exists anyway, but wrapping (vs saturating) makes the failure mode disorienting instead of merely clamped.
evidence: ui.rs:153-156 — `// Count VISUAL rows (post-wrap) at the TRANSCRIPT width, not logical lines.\nlet total = transcript.line_count(transcript_area.width) as u16;\nlet max_off = total.saturating_sub(view_h);`
suggested_fix: Compute in usize and saturate: `let total = transcript.line_count(w).min(u16::MAX as usize) as u16;` so an over-long transcript pins to the newest reachable window instead of wrapping to the top.

title: Daemon HTTP API: wildcard CORS on all responses combined with optional auth exposes task execution to browser drive-by when no tokens are configured
description: Never-audited angle (the 2026-05-06 audit scope was heartbit-core). cors_middleware unconditionally sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on every response and answers preflight for GET/POST/DELETE from any origin. Auth is optional: resolve_auth_tokens (auth.rs:36-49) returns None when no bearer tokens are configured and HEARTBIT_API_KEY is unset, and mod.rs:1244-1253 then merges the protected routes unauthenticated. In that (warned-but-supported) configuration, JavaScript on ANY website the operator visits can POST to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1/tasks and /v1/tasks/execute — which dispatch agent runs with tools (bash, write, etc.) — and, because of the wildcard CORS header, READ the responses (task results, /v1/stats, /v1/usage, SSE streams). Localhost binding does not stop a browser drive-by. Chrome's Private Network Access partially mitigates but Firefox/Safari do not. This is distinct from the accepted bash-jail-escape risk: that concerned the local agent; this is remote-origin web content driving the daemon.
suggested_fix: Restrict the wildcard CORS header to the no-credentials dashboard case AND refuse to start (or restrict Allow-Origin to an explicit configured origin list / localhost origins) when protected routes are mounted without any auth; at minimum gate cors_middleware behind a config flag defaulting to off when auth_tokens.is_none().

title: heartbit-macro: #[tool(default = ...)] on a non-Option parameter advertises a default in the schema but the runtime still requires the field
description: build_schema_tokens inserts the `default` into the JSON schema for any param that carries #[tool(default = ...)] (lines 320-330) but adds the param to `required` whenever it is not Option (lines 339-341). build_deserialize_tokens' non-Option branch (lines 401-414) ignores default_value entirely and errors with 'missing required field'. Net effect: a tool author who writes `#[tool(default = 10)] max_results: u32` produces a schema that tells the LLM the argument is optional-with-default, the model omits it, and the tool call fails at runtime. The documented example uses Option so this is an edge case, but the macro accepts the attribute on non-Option params without complaint, so the contradiction is silent.
suggested_fix: Either emit a compile error when #[tool(default)] is used on a non-Option param, or honor it: skip required_names for defaulted params and fall back to the default in the non-Option deserialize branch.

title: Gateway sensor-triage provider: doc claims haiku, code wires claude-sonnet-4 as the 'SLM'
description: build_slm_provider is documented as a 'lightweight LLM provider for sensor triage ... (using haiku)' but constructs claude-sonnet-4-20250514 on both the Anthropic and OpenRouter paths. Sensor triage runs per ingested event, so this silently runs every triage call on a model roughly an order of magnitude more expensive than the documented intent. Behavior/cost drift, not a crash.
suggested_fix: Pick one: switch the model to a haiku-class model as documented, or fix the doc comment (and ideally make the triage model configurable in gateway.toml).
